q: What time do I show up on my first day and what should I bring?
answer: You should report to the HR office (lower lobby, next to the employee entrance) at 8:30 am. Bring two forms of ID for your I-9 paperwork, your bank details for direct deposit, and closed-toe, non-slip shoes.

q: how many shifts do i shadow before working alone
answer: You must shadow a trainer for at least three shifts before working alone. This is part of your first week.

q: What do I need to pass in my first month?
answer:
By the end of your first 30 days, you need to:

- pass the menu and allergen knowledge check (80% to pass; you may retake it once)
- complete the guest service training "LEARN" (section 5.1)
- have a 30-day review with your manager

If you work in an alcohol-serving position, you also must complete responsible alcohol service certification within 30 days of hire; the resort pays the course fee.

q: When do schedules come out?
answer: Schedules are posted every Wednesday by 5 pm for the following Monday-Sunday week, in the scheduling app and on the board outside the kitchen office. Check your schedule before every shift; changes after posting are sent through the app.

q: Can I just trade shifts with someone?
answer: Yes, with approval. You may swap a shift with a coworker in the same position. Post the swap in the scheduling app; it only counts once your manager approves it. Until it is approved, you are still responsible for the original shift. Swaps that would put either person over 40 hours in a week need manager approval because of overtime.

q: I'm sick, my shift starts at 5pm. When do I need to call?
answer: You need to call the outlet manager's line at least 4 hours before your start time, which for a 5 pm shift means by 1 pm. If you cannot work a shift, call the outlet manager's line at least 4 hours before your start time (2 hours for morning shifts starting before 8 am). Texting a coworker is not a call-out.

q: Is texting my coworker enough to call out?
answer: No, texting a coworker is not a call-out. If you cannot work a shift, call the outlet manager's line at least 4 hours before your start time (2 hours for morning shifts starting before 8 am). Texting a coworker is not a call-out.

q: My buddy said he can clock me in if I'm running late. Is that ok?
answer: No, that's not okay. Never clock in or out for another employee. If you're running late, call before your start time on the outlet manager's line, since texting a coworker is not a call-out. If you forget to clock in, tell your manager the same day so they can fix the punch.

q: I forgot to clock out last night. What should I do?
answer: If you forget to clock in or out, tell your manager the same day so they can fix the punch; do not wait until payday. Also, never clock in or out for another employee.

q: I'm 17. When do I get my lunch break?
answer: Employees under 18 must take a 30-minute meal break after 5 hours of work. Clock out for meal breaks; do not clock out for rest breaks.

q: Do I get paid for my 10 minute break?
answer: Yes. Employees also receive one paid 10-minute rest break for every 4 hours worked. Clock out for meal breaks; do not clock out for rest breaks.

q: When does overtime kick in?
answer: Overtime starts after 40 hours in a week. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times your regular rate for hours over 40 in a Monday-Sunday workweek. All overtime must be approved by your manager in advance.

q: When is payday?
answer: Pay is every other Friday by direct deposit. I couldn't find this in the handbook for the rest, since it doesn't list the specific dates. For pay questions, contact HR at extension 4100, Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm.

q: I'm a busser. How do I get tips?
answer: As a busser, you receive a share of the tip pool rather than keeping tips directly. Servers and bartenders keep their own tips. Bussers, food runners and hosts receive a share of the tip pool: servers contribute 3% of their food and beverage sales, and bartenders contribute 2% of their sales. The pool is paid out with your paycheck. Pay is every other Friday by direct deposit. If your paycheck looks wrong, contact HR within 7 days of payday. You can reach HR at extension 4100.

q: Do managers get a cut of the tip pool?
answer: No, managers don't take part in the tip pool. Managers never take part in the tip pool.

q: I work about 25 hours a week. Can I get medical insurance?
answer: No, part-time employees are not eligible for medical coverage. Full-time employees (averaging 30 or more hours a week) are eligible for medical, dental and vision coverage starting the first of the month after 30 days of employment. Part-time employees are not eligible for medical coverage but may join the retirement savings plan after 90 days. For benefits questions, contact HR at extension 4100, Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm.

q: I want Dec 26 off to see family. Can I request it?
answer: You can submit the request in the scheduling app, but it may be denied. Request time off in the scheduling app at least 3 weeks before the date. Requests are approved first-come, first-served, and may be denied during blackout periods: the week of Christmas through New Year's Day, Easter weekend, and the Fourth of July. Since Dec 26 falls within the Christmas to New Year's Day period, your request may not be approved. Do not book travel until your request is approved.

q: How far ahead do I need to request vacation?
answer: You need to request time off in the scheduling app at least 3 weeks before the date.

q: Do I get extra pay if I work Thanksgiving?
answer: Yes. Employees who work on New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving or Christmas Day are paid 1.5 times their regular rate for hours worked that day. For questions about your pay, contact HR at extension 4100, Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm.

q: A guest is mad their food was cold. Can I comp their whole meal?
answer: No, you can't comp the whole meal on your own. You may offer a complimentary dessert or non-alcoholic drink up to $15 to resolve a complaint. Anything more, including comping a meal or a room charge, needs a manager. Under the LEARN process, you should also notify your manager so they can follow up. Per the Lanai Grill SOPs, comps up to $15 under the LEARN policy (handbook section 5.1) need a manager's approval code in the POS.

q: guest might be having an allergic reaction what do i do
answer: If a guest has an allergic reaction, call security at extension 5555 immediately. Security is trained in first aid and will call 911 if needed. Do not move an injured person unless they are in danger.

q: Someone looks about 35. Do I need to card them?
answer: Yes. Check ID for anyone who looks under 40. Accept only valid, unexpired government photo IDs. Someone who looks 35 falls under that rule.

q: Can I wear sneakers?
answer: The handbook requires black, closed-toe, non-slip shoes in all F&B areas. It doesn't say whether sneakers meet that standard, so I couldn't find this in the handbook for the rest. Check with your manager before wearing them on shift.

q: I hurt my hand at work but it's minor. Do I need to report it?
answer: Yes. If you are injured at work, tell your manager right away, even if it seems minor, and complete an incident report before the end of your shift.

q: How do I report harassment anonymously?
answer: You can report harassment anonymously through the Ethics Line at 1-800-555-0199 (a fictitious number for this sample). Harassment or discrimination of any kind is not tolerated. Report it to your manager, to HR, or anonymously through the Ethics Line at 1-800-555-0199 (a fictitious number for this sample). You will not be punished for reporting in good faith.

q: Where do employees park and how much is it?
answer: Employees park in the employee lot on Example Beach Road, not in the guest garage. A monthly employee parking pass costs $25 through payroll deduction; sign up with HR.

q: Can I eat the leftover buffet food after brunch?
answer: No. Employees may not eat food from the kitchen, buffet or guest areas, including leftovers. One free meal is provided per shift in the employee cafeteria.

q: What temp does the walk-in need to be?
answer: The walk-in should be at or below 41°F. Cold food must be held at 41°F or below; hot food at 135°F or above. Check and log walk-in cooler and freezer temperatures at opening and closing on the clipboard by the door. If it reads above 41°F, tell the chef or MOD immediately and do not serve food from it until it is checked.

q: Can I void an item after I sent it to the kitchen?
answer: No, servers cannot void an item after it has been sent to the kitchen. Ask a manager to void it and give the reason (kitchen error, guest changed mind, etc.).

q: My drawer is $3 short. Do I have to report it?
answer: The Lanai Grill SOPs require you to report any shortage over $5 to the manager before clocking out. A $3 shortage is under that threshold, so the SOP doesn't require you to report it. I couldn't find this in the handbook for the rest, including whether you should still tell your manager about a shortage under $5.
